title: M5: Mastering Page Migration and Memory Management for CXL-based Tiered Memory Systems
problem: CXL DRAM has 2-3x higher access latency than DDR DRAM, requiring effective page migration between tiers. Existing CPU-driven page-migration solutions misclassify warm pages as hot pages, fail to handle sparse hot-word pages (where only a small fraction of words in a page are hot), and incur high profiling overhead that can itself degrade application performance.
motivation: CXL memory is emerging as a cost-effective capacity expansion for memory systems, but the latency gap between DDR and CXL tiers demands precise hot-page identification and migration that current CPU-driven solutions cannot provide.
method: M5 puts access counters directly in the CXL hardware controller, where they track which 4KB pages and which 64-byte chunks within those pages get accessed most often. Unlike CPU-based approaches that guess at hot pages by counting page faults (which often misidentifies warm pages as hot), the CXL controller sees every actual access. When it finds that only certain chunks within a page get used frequently, it can move just those chunks to faster memory instead of moving the entire page—avoiding unnecessary movement.
key_novelty: Embed access counters in the CXL hardware controller—rather than having the CPU guess via page faults—so it can precisely track which 64-byte chunks get used frequently and selectively move only the hot chunks instead of entire pages.
contributions: Discovery that CPU-driven page-migration solutions frequently misclassify warm pages as hot pages
Identification and characterization of sparse hot-page applications where sub-page hot-word migration is needed
M5 platform with hardware-based hot-page and hot-word trackers in the CXL controller
47% hotter pages identified and 14% higher performance than the best CPU-driven solution with a simple policy

metrics.speedup: 14% higher performance than best CPU-driven page migration solution

baselines: CPU-driven page-migration solutions (perf-counter based, OS page-fault sampling)
limitations: Evaluation with a simple policy; more sophisticated policies enabled by the hardware may yield larger gains; hardware tracker area and power overhead not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: CXL-controller hardware hot-page and hot-word tracking for precise tiered memory migration
